about: THE SHIPS AS BODIES (Design/ship_physics.md 2.1): the numbers the ship's body is built from - size and shape, weights and where they sit, how she swings, how the water holds her back, her oars. Read by Kapman.Ships.ShipClassData; checked by the Ship*Tests. Converted 4 Oct 2026 from the first build's Assets/Kapman/Game/Data/ship_classes_793.json (size, crew, cargo, oars, from/to) with the ship physics document's columns added. Numbers marked (guess) in the notes have no source behind them; (derived) ones are computed from the others.

units.from, to: years on the water; 0 = before the game / no end (the first build's convention)
units.status: in_use = sailed in the game now; later = kept for a hull that is not in the game yet
units.length_m, beam_m: overall length and the beam at the waterline (m)
units.lwl_m, depth_m, draught_m: length on the waterline, depth from keel to gunwale amidships, laden draught (m)
units.cb, section_q: block coefficient; section shape: the section fills as (d/T)^q from the keel (1 a flat box, 1.5 a round bilge); cb x q must not pass 1
units.*_kg, *_cg_m: masses and their heights above the keel (m); crew = men aboard at man_kg each
units.k_roll_m, k_pitch_m, k_yaw_m: radii of gyration of the laden ship (m)
units.added_mass: added-mass coefficients on each axis (a share of her mass or inertia that the water adds)
units.heave_damping_ratio: share of critical damping in heave (ship physics 2.2: heave and roll die in 2-3 cycles)
units.heave_drag_cd: drag coefficient of the hull's bottom moving up and down (the quadratic part of the damping)
units.lateral_area_m2, lateral_cd: the hull's side area under water at the laden draught, and its cross-flow drag coefficient
units.cr_fn, cr: the residuary resistance coefficient against the Froude number (ship physics 2.4; test 6 fits it, night two)
units.oar_*: oars (both sides), a man's sustained watts, the oar's efficiency, the most an oar pulls at the catch (N), the turning torque of the oars on one side (N m)
units.steering_oar_*: the steering oar's blade area (m2) and its arm aft of the centre of gravity (m)
units.gm_m: metacentric height laden (m), from the parametric probe cells: the tests hold the code to it within 10 percent
units.hs_limit_m: the significant wave height she should not be out in (m)
units.sheer_m: how much higher the gunwale stands at the stem and stern than amidships (m): the ends' margin before green water comes over (ship physics 2.8)
units.windage_m2: the hull's and the bare mast's side-on area in the wind (m2; head-on about a third of it): what the wind pushes at anchor, hove to and under oars (ship physics 2.6, 2.9)
units.leak_m3_per_h: what a sound hull lets in through the laps in still water (m3 an hour); working in a sea multiplies it (ship physics 2.8)
units.plank_limit_ms: the contact speed on gravel or rock that cracks a plank (m/s; twice it stoves one in) (ship physics 2.1, 2.9)
units.vanishing_beyond_flood_deg: how far past the downflooding angle (the gunwale at the water) she still comes back (degrees): past it she is over (ship physics 2.5, 2.8)
units.anchor_kg, anchor_kind: the anchor's weight and kind: iron (fluked, with a wooden stock) or stone (ship physics 2.9)
units.rode_m, rode_strength_n: the anchor rope's length (m) and what it bears new, wet and spliced (N) before it parts (ship physics 2.9)

classes.name: Gislinge boat (the player's boat)
sources: Viking Ship Museum, the Gislinge boat open-source project (https://www.vikingeskibsmuseet.dk/en/professions/boatyard/the-gislinge-boat-open-source-project): 7.7 x 1.5 m, about 1 t of cargo ('four men and ten sheep'), c. 1130
ship_classes_793.json row 'gislinge': 6 oars, crew 4 (the user's decision of 2026-10-01), cargo 0.9 t, from/to 0/0
Design/ship_physics.md 1.1 and 2.1: LWL 6.8, depth 0.6, hull 500 kg, CG 0.25 m, Cb 0.5, radii 0.4 B and 0.25 L, added mass, the C_r table, the oars' 90 W and 0.55, the steering oar, Hs limit 1.2 m
uncertain: LATER: built c. 1130, a stand-in for the small boats of 793 (decision 5: the Gislinge first, Dorestat 1's numbers dropped in later)

draught 0.35 m (derived): 1,820 kg laden (hull 500 + 4 men 320 + gear 100 + cargo 900) at Cb 0.5 on 6.8 x 1.5 m; the first build's 0.25 m draught with 0.34 m freeboard would need Cb 0.69, too full for her fine ends
GM 0.52 m (derived from the cells; the design document guessed 0.35 laden); her roll period 1.9 s matches its derivation
hull mass, the heights of the weights, Cb, the radii, added mass, damping, side area, C_r, oar figures: (guess) as in Design/ship_physics.md

night two and three (4 Oct): sheer 0.25 m and windage 3.0 m2 (guess: the design's 0.6 L (freeboard + 0.3) gives 2.5 m2, its anchor sum uses 3.5); leak 0.002 m3/h, plank limit 1.5 m/s, vanishing 25 deg past the downflooding angle, a 15 kg iron anchor and 10 kN for the wet 16 mm rope (Design/ship_physics.md 2.8-2.9, all guesses there); a 30 m rope (guess)

classes.name: Dorestat 1 (stand-in numbers: the 14 m coaster)
sources: Design/ship_physics.md 1.1 and 2.1: the 14 m coaster (Graveney / Skuldelev 3 class) that stands in for Dorestat 1: 14 x 3.6 x 1.35 m, LWL 12.5, hull 3.5 t, CG 0.5 m, Cb 0.48, radii, 4 oars, steering oar 0.35 m2 at 6 m, Hs limit 2.5 m
Skuldelev 3 (Roar Ege): 14 x 3.3 x 0.9 m, 9.6 t displacement, 4.6 t cargo, 5 oar ports (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skuldelev_ships)
uncertain: NOT Dorestat 1's own measurements: the excavation report or the 2021 replica's page is still to be found and cited (Design/ship_physics.md 5); until then this row is the 14 m coaster's numbers and is not sailed (status later)
draught 0.42 m (derived): 9,280 kg laden (hull 3,500 + 6 men 480 + gear 300 + cargo 5,000) at Cb 0.48 on 12.5 x 3.6 m; the design document's ~0.75 m would need 16.6 t
GM 2.6 m (derived from the cells) is far above the design document's 0.7 m guess: the waterline beam is taken as the full 3.6 m and the draught is shallow; settle it with Dorestat 1's own lines
side area 6.5 m2 (derived: 12.5 m x 0.42 m x 0.85 plus a 0.15 m keel); oar turning torque 216 N m (derived: two oars a side at 60 N on a 1.8 m arm); the rest (guess) as in Design/ship_physics.md

night two and three (4 Oct): windage 10 m2 (derived: 0.6 x 14 x (0.93 + 0.3), rounded up for the mast); sheer 0.45 m, leak 0.004 m3/h, a 40 kg iron anchor and a 60 m rope of 20 kN (guess: between the design's 10 kN small-boat and 35 kN knarr ropes); plank limit 1.8 m/s (Design/ship_physics.md 2.1)
